audit.whatIsWrong: Six chart rows disagreed with the packet chart and the mirror: Level 1 read 'Skill' and Level 2 'Renekton' (the reverse of the real shape — whys[1] itself calls Level 2 a coin flip), and Levels 4-5, Level 6 and both item rows gave you the lane while whys[3], whys[5] and whys[6] describe Gragas taking it.
audit.why: 49.52% over 1561 games. Packet chart and mirror (gragas__renekton) both read Renekton / Skill / Renekton / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 flipped in matched full/content pairs; ratings re-spread 6/5/7/4/4/3/3.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item row credited your Eclipse; spikes[2] on the same page says Gragas's first AP component is what flips the sustain check. The 2+-item row claimed your side-lane pattern is at full power against an AP Gragas the page says out-sustains you.
audit.why: Happy Hour heals on every skill cast and Drunken Rage cuts incoming damage — both scale with his items, not yours.
audit.corrected: phases[3].why, phases[5].why and phases[6].why rewritten to the real spike order.

audit.whatIsWrong: Drunken Rage was never named on the full layer even though it is the interaction that decides every trade: it is a 1-second sip that both reduces damage he receives and loads an auto-attack reset, so the sip — not his engage — is the tell. Body Slam's real cooldown (14s at rank 1, only 12s at rank 5) was never given, and Barrel Roll's ramping potency was reduced to 'his Q puddle'.
audit.why: Gragas W: 'samples his latest brew for 1 second ... dealing magic damage to all nearby enemies on his next basic attack and reducing damage received', 5s. E: 14/13.5/13/12.5/12. Q: 'The potency of the explosion increases over time', 4s fuse.
audit.corrected: The sip tell stated in report[5].t, the 14s cooldown in dosFull[0].d, the ramping cask in dontsFull[1].d.

audit.why: Happy Hour heals on every cast, and report[8].t already buys Executioner's Calling early with the reason stated.

edits.before: Fury autos bully the first waves. Identify how Gragas contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Fury autos bully wave one — Barrel Roll costs 80 mana and he has no dash until 3, so step up and chip.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Body Slam's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Drunken Rage now eats a chunk of your empowered W and Body Slam takes him out on 14s — the damage check flips against you.

edits.before: Eclipse is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Body Slam's cooldown.
edits.after: His first AP item turns Happy Hour into real sustain — your Eclipse burst stops closing.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Gragas carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: AP Gragas mitigates physical burst with W and sets up kills with Body Slam into Cask — play with your team, not the side lane.

edits.before: His engage. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His engage and his exit, 14s at rank 1 — fight on the whiff.

edits.before: Track Gragas's Body Slam: His engage. Bait it. When it is down — W-stun + Q him.
edits.after: Drunken Rage cuts your damage and resets his auto — that 1s sip is your cue to step off.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Barrel Roll gets stronger the longer it sits — leave before it pops.

notes: Mirror reported the content layer here was already accurate and the damage was all in the full layer; that matched what I found — the whys and spikes named the right abilities while the full layer was template text with no numbers. Chart proposed as one atomic group across both layers.
